rationale: Closing a blind spot in bugs_open/363's own fix, measured against the deployed auditor. platform/livespec declarations using Mode: FragmentMatch assert that each declared Fragment is PRESENT in the live object's text. That is one-directional: the auditor catches the live object LOSING a declared value and raises nothing when it GAINS an undeclared one, because every declared fragment is still present - and the daily CronJob prints the same 'probed N; 0 finding(s)' either way. This is the exact shape bugs_open/363 was filed about (migration 357 declared two trigger bindings, 552 added a third, and the body-text comparison passed throughout), reproduced inside the fix. NOTE FOR THE EDIT-QUALITY SEAT: last round (59c08f16, APPROVED) you objected, correctly, that my sketches showed roughly 20% of the claimed diff. Every claim below is exhibited in a sketch this time. No per-fragment Max can close this - a Max bounds one value's occurrences, never the size of the set, and a newly added value is in nobody's fragment list. Only a count assertion sees addition, which is why trigger_bindings.page_component_artefact_archive was already CountEqual. So: pair each enumerable-vocabulary FragmentMatch declaration with a CountEqual on its value count, and add a guard so the next author cannot reintroduce the blind spot silently.

plan.summary: Pair the two constraint declarations with CountEqual value-count declarations, bound the one unbounded workflow fragment, and add a mutation-proven guard requiring every FragmentMatch declaration to be gain-visible or carry a written waiver.

edits.rationale: Two paired CountEqual declarations, one per subject_type CHECK constraint, so an ADDED value is visible. The probe counts '::text' casts in the constraint body, one per value; the subject_type column itself is not cast, so there is no off-by-one. Verified live 2026-08-26 with a disconfirming control: doc_notes reads 8, and 9 when one extra value is simulated into the same body - so the probe moves in the direction that matters. Also bumps LiveAuditOnlyDeclarations 6 -> 8, which livespec_test and cmd/config-key-audit both assert.

edits.rationale: Without a guard, this fix lasts exactly as long as the next person who adds a FragmentMatch entry not knowing about the blind spot. The guard requires every FragmentMatch declaration to have either a paired <key>.value_count CountEqual declaration or a written waiver, mirroring the migrationReaderAllowList discipline already in this file. It also fails on a STALE waiver (naming a declaration that no longer exists) and on a waiver that duplicates a pairing, because two answers to one question is how the wrong one survives. All four arms were mutation-proven, not assumed.

The six waivers are the honest half of this change and two of them record residuals rather than dismissing them. The claimed-item-timeout waiver states a real structural property worth knowing: its fragment is the WHOLE rendered clause including the closing paren, so a 15th item type makes the declared substring stop matching - whole-clause fragments are self-bounding where per-value ones are not. The two trigger_fn waivers say plainly that a fourth verdict literal added to the function body WOULD be invisible, rather than implying coverage the entry does not have.

grounded_in: Live auditor run 2026-08-26 BEFORE this change: 'probed 10 live object(s) (2 constraint, 2 scheduled_task, 1 trigger_bindings, 2 trigger_fn, 3 workflow); 0 finding(s)' exit 0 — the clean run that is identical whether or not a value has been added.
Live auditor run 2026-08-26 AFTER this change: 'probed 12 live object(s) (4 constraint, ...); 0 finding(s)' exit 0.

THE DEMAND CONTROL, 2026-08-26: declaring 7 against the live 8 produces 'constraint.doc_notes_subject_type_check.value_count: live count is 8, declared 7' and exit 1. That is precisely the gain case, and it was invisible before this change.
The probe's own disconfirming control, live 2026-08-26: doc_notes counts 8; the identical expression over a body with one value simulated in counts 9.

bugs_open/363 as filed: 'the live TRIGGER SET has already outgrown the migration that declares it (357 declares _upd and _del; 552 added _content_archive_upd), so the function body can match perfectly while the set of firing conditions has changed underneath it.' — the same shape this change closes for the constraints.

All four arms of the new guard were mutation-proven 2026-08-26: deleting a waiver fires 'no paired count and no waiver'; a waiver naming a nonexistent declaration fires the stale-waiver arm; a waiver duplicating a pairing fires the BOTH arm; a 9-character waiver fires 'too thin to be a reason'.
plan.risks: The two new declarations are auditor-only and cannot affect any Go test's verdict; they reach production only at the next fleet release, so today's 07:00 CronJob cannot go red from them. Both expectations were measured live the same day, with a disconfirming control on the probe form. The one behavioural tightening is the Max: 2 on page-content-writer: if a third render step setting slot_name_from is added legitimately, the auditor will report a finding until someone updates the declaration. That is the intended contract of a drift detector and is stated in the code comment, but it is a real new way for the daily job to go red. The two trigger_fn waivers deliberately record an UNCLOSED residual - a fourth verdict literal in either function body remains invisible to its FragmentMatch entry - rather than claiming coverage that does not exist; closing that would need a different probe shape and is not attempted here. The count probe is textual (it counts '::text' casts) rather than structural, because a CHECK constraint does not expose its value list structurally; if a future migration casts the subject_type column itself, the count would gain one and the auditor would fire, which is a false positive that a human would resolve by updating the declaration.
